claims.text: NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys are rare-earth-free materials with magnetocaloric behavior.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations generate localized magnetic clusters.
Exchange interactions among localized magnetic clusters enable nearly reversible magnetic transitions at low applied fields.
The proposed cluster-mediated magnetic behavior preserves rapid heat exchange.
NiFeCoCr-based materials possess mechanical properties favorable for stability and manufacturability.
The initial NiFeCoCr-based alloy is predominantly BCC.
The initial alloy inherently contains nanoscale compositional fluctuations.
The controlled intervention is to replace a small fraction of Ni with Cu while retaining the baseline alloy for comparison.
Compositional additions can tune the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of the parent NiFeCoCr alloy.
Replacing Ni with Cu changes electron concentration and thereby changes magnetic-cluster size and distribution.
The magnetic clusters mediate local exchange interactions and domain reorientation.
Tuning cluster extent and interaction strength reduces the energy barriers for field-induced magnetic reorientation.
Reduced reorientation barriers produce lower coercivity and reduced hysteresis.
The substitution causes the peak magnetic entropy change to occur at a lower applied field.
The substituted alloy retains thermal-transfer efficiency relative to the baseline.
The substituted alloy retains mechanical integrity relative to the baseline.
The hypothesis applies near room temperature, where the transition temperature of NiFeCoCr-based alloys can be compositionally tuned.
The mechanism is restricted to a predominantly single-phase BCC regime with nanoscale fluctuations and may fail after phase separation.
